newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Slovak blue chips mixed as SAX backs off year-high.
newsitem.headline: Slovak blue chips mixed as SAX backs off year-high.

text.p: Major Slovak shares closed mixed in moderate trading on the Bratislava Stock Exchange (BSE) on Tuesday, as the SAX index backed off Monday's year-high.
The SAX closed down 0.18 points at 202.44, but brokers said it appeared to be only a technical break from its three-week uptrend.
"I think the rise, regarding at least the most liquid issues on the BSE, has not yet stopped," Radovan Dzugas of Creditanstalt said.
Steel maker VSZ traded the biggest volume on the bourse's listed floor, closing up four crowns at 710 with 8,002 traded shares.
"Shares of VSZ seem to be well-supported by confidence of long-term investors at the present, as the issue traded some 50,000 shares in total at around 710 crowns in last several days," Dzugas said.
He said oil refiner Slovnaft has been another leading issue boosting the overall market's performance, with strong interest in the share shown by long-term investors.

Dzugas said the bad performance of oil and gas storage firm Nafta, which eased 10 crowns to 1,650, was caused mainly by a negative campaign over the new company's management, since it was privatised in last summer.
"There are some stakes offered for sale in Nafta from abroad, but at a loss-price," he added.
Overall volume decreased to 512,257 shares, from 774,064 shares traded on Monday, while turnover eased to 452.52 million crowns, from 472.45 million.
